title: Ordered grip curvature did not establish added lifting-difficulty prediction across independent NHANES samples
abstract: A fixed logistic model fitted in 1,407 NHANES 2011–2012 participants aged at least 60 was transferred to 1,503 participants in the separately released 2013–2014 survey sample. Adding the bilateral mean normalized second difference of three grip trials to demographic, adiposity, strength, asymmetry, variability and signed-change measures changed weighted target log loss by -0.000245 (conditional 95% stratified-PSU bootstrap interval -0.001321 to 0.000742; source-and-target refit interval -0.001355 to 0.003520). AUROC changed by -0.000903. Source-only cross-validation also worsened. The prespecified incremental-prediction criterion was not met. This is a negative test of one ordered representation, not evidence that trial dynamics lack physiological information. Validation uses distinct survey-cycle samples under the same protocol, not a different institution or clinical cohort.
